articles.title: The Developer's Field Guide to Google DevFest Atlanta 2026
articles.excerpt: One question stayed with me after Google DevFest Atlanta 2026 at Morehouse College: if an AI agent needed to stop right now, could your team prove that it stopped safely? Jim Stephens's session on the…
articles.body: One question stayed with me after Google DevFest Atlanta 2026 at Morehouse College: if an AI agent needed to stop right now, could your team prove that it stopped safely? A lot of the conversation around agentic AI is still focused on how quickly we can build, connect, and automate. But several sessions at DevFest pushed in a different direction: what does it actually take to operate these systems safely once they are doing real work? Jim Stephens's session on the Hidden Constraint Index gave a practical way to think about what is really slowing an organization down. The key reminder for me was that the first diagnosis is not always the real constraint. A team can optimize for speed or adoption and still create problems elsewhere in the system.
articles.author: Tiru Naidu

articles.title: I built the API that published my 5 books on Amazon KDP
articles.excerpt: I'm a solo dev. I also write nonfiction books — ancient scripture, Apollo, declassified aerospace records, that corner of the shelf. I have five of them live on Amazon KDP as paperbacks right now. The…
articles.body: I'm a solo dev. I also write nonfiction books — ancient scripture, Apollo, declassified aerospace records, that corner of the shelf. I have five of them live on Amazon KDP as paperbacks right now. The part nobody warns you about isn't the writing. It's the formatting. Specifically: turning a manuscript into an EPUB 3 file that doesn't embarrass you on a Kindle. The pain Every book meant the same miserable checklist: Metadata — title, author, identifiers, language, all in the right XML, or retailers mangle your listing. The OPF manifest — every single file in the book (every chapter, every image, every stylesheet) declared in content.opf , in order, spelled exactly right. Miss one and the whole archive is invalid. The NCX table of contents — the navigation file Kindle actually uses.
articles.author: J Singerman

articles.title: I counted every subreddit since 2005, and "how many" depends on one definition
articles.excerpt: If you've ever tried to answer "how many subreddits are there?", you know the numbers online don't agree with each other. I wanted to know why, so I ran the count myself on every public Reddit post an…
articles.body: If you've ever tried to answer "how many subreddits are there?", you know the numbers online don't agree with each other. I wanted to know why, so I ran the count myself on every public Reddit post and comment going back to the start. The answer I got wasn't one number. It was three, and the gap between them is huge. Here's what the same platform looks like through three different definitions: What you count Subreddits Ever had a post, since 2005 7,844,766 Had a post or comment in September 2026 388,172 Had 10+ posts by people in September 2026 122,833 You can quote any row of that table and be technically right. That's the part I find interesting as someone who works with data, because the hard question isn't the counting at all.
articles.author: Dmytro Krutytskyi

articles.title: Is CVE-2026-98432 Patched in Ubuntu 24.04? Latest Update
articles.excerpt: Is CVE-2026-98432 Patched in Ubuntu 24.04? Latest Update CVE-2026-98432 is not yet patched in Ubuntu 24.04. Ubuntu currently lists the release as vulnerable, with a fix in progress for the Linux kerne…
articles.body: Is CVE-2026-98432 Patched in Ubuntu 24.04? Latest Update CVE-2026-98432 is not yet patched in Ubuntu 24.04. Ubuntu currently lists the release as vulnerable, with a fix in progress for the Linux kernel package version 6.8.0-149.149 . The vulnerability affects the Linux kernel’s IPv4 TCP networking code and may allow a remote attacker to execute commands with root privileges. The risk is particularly serious for servers using Multipath TCP, also known as MPTCP. What is CVE-2026-98432? CVE-2026-98432 is a critical Linux kernel vulnerability involving a use-after-free flaw in IPv4 TCP processing. This type of flaw occurs when the kernel continues using memory after it has already been released.
articles.author: Anointed

articles.title: Stopping Is a Capability: What Two Governance Talks at Google DevFest Atlanta 2026 Had in Common
articles.excerpt: Attending Google DevFest Atlanta 2026 at Morehouse College left me with one question worth taking into the boardroom: If one of your AI systems needed to stop right now, could you prove to a regulator…
articles.body: Attending Google DevFest Atlanta 2026 at Morehouse College left me with one question worth taking into the boardroom: If one of your AI systems needed to stop right now, could you prove to a regulator, customer, or your own board that it stopped safely? Jim Stephens's session on the Hidden Constraint Index highlighted an important leadership challenge: the pace of innovation can move faster than an organization's capacity to absorb and execute it. Individual teams may optimize successfully for speed, but that does not automatically mean the organization as a whole is moving effectively. That is not simply an engineering problem. It is also a question of governance, incentives, ownership, and organizational capacity.
articles.author: Tiru Naidu

articles.body: Find and replace is one of those jobs that quietly sends your file to somebody else's server. You paste a config file, a customer list, or a draft with a name in it, and the words come back changed - because the text was uploaded on the way. Text Studio does the same job inside the tab you already have open. I work on OnePassApps, the team behind the app. Find and replace is one of eight tools on the Text Studio page. This post is about the mechanics rather than the pitch: what the panel actually offers, what its defaults do, and how to read the result so you know the replacement really happened.

articles.title: James Webb Space Telescope uncovers new clues about the origins of 'interstellar invader' comet 3I/ATLAS
articles.excerpt: The findings are another clue towards understanding the origins of 3I/ATLAS and the planet-forming conditions around other stars.
articles.body: Using the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), scientists have found that the interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS was built from tiny grains of ice mixed with dust that are quite different from the solar system’s comets. These ice grains do, however, bear striking similarities to some icy bodies located at the edge of the solar system, beyond the orbit of Neptune, so-called trans-Neptunian objects (TNOs). 3I/ATLAS was discovered entering the solar system in the summer of 2025. It was only the third object found entering the solar system from farther afield in the Milky Way after 1I/'Oumuamua , seen in 2017, and 2I/Borisov , detected in 2019. This meant the interstellar comet offered a rare chance to glimpse the conditions under which such bodies form in other star systems.

articles.title: Raising the quality of insights in agentic analytics
articles.excerpt: In just a few years, generative AI has changed the face of enterprise analytics, notably by making analytics accessible to users across the organization. Agentic AI promises to do even more, by automa…
articles.body: In just a few years, generative AI has changed the face of enterprise analytics, notably by making analytics accessible to users across the organization. Agentic AI promises to do even more, by automating entire workflows and taking actions based on agent insights. But there is a problem: The quality of insights that agents currently generate leaves much to be desired. Fewer than half of agent-generated insights at the organizations surveyed for this report lead to business improvement. And while most respondents praise the quality of their agents’ descriptive insights, reviews of their prescriptive insights—those on which actions are based—are decidedly mixed.
